item.title: System Design for a Go Web App on AWS
item.description:
System Design for a Go Web App on AWS

Building and deploying a Go web application on AWS is more than just spinning up a server and pointing a domain. In this post, we’ll walk through a real-world-ready system design with a focus on IAM, Security Groups, inter-service communication, and replication. Let’s break it down from DNS to database — the secure and scalable way.

Application Recap

We’re working with a Go web server exposing an HTTP API. Think net/http, chi, or gin. It talks to a database, serves some static files, and might upload images or documents.

item.title: Understanding Logging and Observability in Modern Applications
item.description:
Building reliable applications goes beyond writing code that works. As systems grow in complexity, understanding what’s happening inside your application becomes critical. This is where logging and observability come in. In this post, we’ll explore these concepts, why they matter, and how you can improve them in your projects.

What Is Logging?

Logging is the practice of recording events, errors, and other runtime information from your application. These records, or logs, are crucial for understanding system behavior and diagnosing issues.
